title: RTP dissector: Removed unused functions
description: Removed unused functions found by Martin Mathieson.

notes.body:
These functions were introduced by Hadriel Kaplan in 2014 (git log -p 04c05a21e34cec326f1aff2f5f8a6e74e1ced984), and there were no calls to them in that change itself.

I don't know of, and couldn't find any reference to, a process for deprecating functions.

Can you think of a place where it would make sense to call these functions?

My point of view:
rtp_dyn_payload functions are used during SDP processing in many parts of Wireshark. I think that functions were created as part of "CRUD" approach. Unused functions allow replace and delete a value from hash table, but replace and delete was never used.
When SDP is processed, you can use delete probably when you renegotiate codecs, but in real you do not need to delete unused codec from hash because this entry will not be used anymore in the call. At the end of the call, values are not deleted one by one, but released by free all together.
Replace can be used again during SDP processing, but usually second or subsequent SDP uses same IDs for same codec therefore you don't have to call replace because values are same.
So I think that they are really useless.
I think we should just delete those functions completely then.
